name: Fe-C

suspended_phases.M7C3_D101: Left out: its parameters are attributed only to an unidentified "This work" (REF1) in the database file. It is never stable below x(C) = 0.25, so leaving it out does not change the displayed diagram.
suspended_phases.DIAMOND_A4: Left out: diamond is stable only at high pressure. At 1 atm it is always less stable than graphite, so it never appears in the stable diagram; with graphite suspended (the metastable Fe-Fe3C diagram) ferrite + diamond would replace ferrite + Fe3C below 589 °C, which is not the Fe-Fe3C diagram of steel practice.

diagram_note: Temperatures and compositions are this assessed database's values (e.g. eutectoid 726.5 °C, 0.76 wt% C); they may differ slightly from older textbook figures.
_source: Assessed Fe-C description of Hallstedt et al. (2010), with the equation of state of Brosh et al. (2007), from pycalphad's test database cfe_broshe.tdb.

citations.text: B. Hallstedt, D. Djurovic, J. von Appen, R. Dronskowski, A. Dick, F. Koermann, T. Hickel, J. Neugebauer, Calphad 34 (2010) 129-133.
Brosh et al., CALPHAD 31 (2007) 173-185 (equation of state; not used at 1 atm beyond its contribution at that pressure).
Database file: pycalphad 0.11.2 test database cfe_broshe.tdb.
